chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Yahya Kawkab al-Dam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The disciples of Isa (peace be upon him) were his Shites, and our Shites are our disciples, and the disciple of Isa was not more obedient to him than our Shites are to us.
And indeed, Isa (peace be upon him) said to the disciples: 'Who will be my helpers in Allah's way?' The disciples said: 'We are helpers of Allah.'
So, by Allah, they did not help him against the Jews, nor did they fight for him.

And our Shites, by Allah, have not ceased since Allah Captured His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to help us, and fight for us, and be burnt, and tortured, and displaced in the cities. May Allah recompense them goodly from us.

And indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, even if I were to strike the noses of those who love us with the sword, they would not hate us, and by Allah, if I were to approach those who hate us and urge them with wealth, they would not love us.'
ai.seo_question: How does the obedience of the Shia compare to the disciples of Jesus according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the theological concept of 'Hawariyyun' (disciples) for the Shia, contrasting their active, enduring support and martyrdom against the relative passivity of Jesus's disciples. It underscores the Shia identity as defined by steadfast loyalty (wilayah) amidst persecution, a theme central to Imam Ali’s description of the unwavering love of the faithful versus the transactional nature of their enemies' affection.

Even if I<sup>asws</sup> were to strike the noses of those who love us<sup>asws</sup> with the sword, they will not hate us<sup>asws</sup>, and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, if I<sup>asws</sup> were to approach those that hate us<sup>asws</sup> and urge them by the wealth they will still not love us<sup>asws</sup>’.
